subject: Residency and deletion alignment for StellarCloud marketplace listing
messages:
From: Devon Price <devon.price@stellarc.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: marketplace-legal@aws-partners.com
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Residency and deletion alignment for StellarCloud marketplace listing

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles. We're moving toward listing Redwood on the StellarCloud marketplace and need to finalize residency/retention language for our marketplace listing and legal review. A few questions from our side: 

1) If a customer chooses an AWS, GCP or Azure region during purchase, where exactly will customer data (input text, embeddings, and billing/usage metadata) be stored by Redwood? Are there differences by cloud vendor?

2) What are the default retention periods for (a) request logs (request/response payloads), (b) model cache/kv cache state, and (c) billing/usage records? Can these be configured per-customer in a marketplace flow?

3) Deletion: what is the expected end-to-end timeline from customer-initiated deletion to irreversible removal from all Redwood systems (including backups and any analytics stores)? Will we get an audit event we can show to our compliance team?

4) For the marketplace listing we need a short attestable statement we can show to customers about data residency (e.g., "All production inference data remains in the region selected by the customer and is not replicated outside the selected cloud region except for aggregated billing metrics"). Can you provide suggested wording and any caveats?

We attached our onboarding checklist with the marketplace legal playbook (attachment: StellarCloud_Marketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf) — legal is waiting for Redwood's answers so they can sign off. Could you loop in security/product folks if needed?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our publishing slot is the week of June 29.

Best,
Devon
Director, Cloud Partnerships
StellarCloud

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Price <devon.price@stellarc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion alignment for StellarCloud marketplace listing

Hi Devon — thanks for the clear list. Putting answers inline and attaching our short options summary (attachment: redwood-residency-options-20260618.pdf).

1) Region mapping: when a customer provisions via the StellarCloud marketplace we honor the region they select and route inference requests to Redwood capacity in that same cloud region (we currently have supported regions across AWS, GCP, and Azure). Non-production telemetry (aggregated metrics, model performance summaries) may be copied to our central analytics region (US-West) — we can disable that for marketplace listings on a per-account basis.

2) Retention defaults and configurability: 
- Request logs (full request/response payloads): default 30 days, configurable down to 0 days for customers who opt for reduced telemetry.
- Model KV cache: ephemeral for serving; cache persists only for the active inference pool and is flushed on redeploy or explicit admin purge. We never treat KV cache as long-term storage for customer data.
- Billing/usage records: retained for 7 years for invoicing/audit purposes by default, but we can provide a minimized export that redacts raw payloads for marketplace customers if needed.

All of the above can be configured during onboarding for marketplace customers; we can expose a preset in the StellarCloud flow (e.g., "Marketplace - Data Minimal", "Marketplace - Standard").

3) Deletion timeline: for most configurations, a customer-initiated deletion request triggers: 
- immediate stop of access (token revoked), 
- background sweep that deletes request logs and cache references within 24–72 hours, and 
- removal from analytics pipelines within 30 days. Backups are on a 90-day rotation; we mark deleted records for purge and they are not returned to production after deletion — full irreversible removal across all systems is typically within 90–120 days depending on the chosen backup/store SLA. We produce a signed deletion event and an audit record that you can present to your compliance team. 

4) Suggested marketplace wording (short):
"Redwood Inference processes inference requests in the cloud region selected by the customer. Request payloads and inference outputs are stored only in the selected region except where explicitly routed to centralized, aggregate analytics (which can be disabled on request). Deletion requests trigger an audit-backed removal workflow; final irreversible deletion may take up to 120 days to account for backup cycles."

Please let us know if StellarCloud needs any stricter guarantees (e.g., 30-day irreversible deletion). If so, we can propose a scoped SLA and update the onboarding flow.

Next steps: Marissa, can you confirm the backup/purge windows and whether we can offer a 30-day irreversible deletion option for marketplace customers (this would be a higher-tier offering)?

Thanks — I can convert the wording into a short attestation for your listing once we lock the timelines.

— Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Devon Price <devon.price@stellarc.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-19T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion alignment for StellarCloud marketplace listing

Adding technical detail from product/security: 

- Data at rest: inference payloads are written to ephemeral caches local to the serving pool in the selected region. Persisted artifacts (request logs) are stored in object storage provisioned in the same region by default. Billing/usage meta (aggregates) are stored in our billing datastore; raw payloads are not moved there.

- Backups: object storage snapshots are retained according to the customer's tier. For the standard marketplace flow snapshots are retained for 90 days - they are encrypted with a region-specific KMS key.

- Deletion sweep: when we receive a deletion API call or marketplace deletion webhook we: 
  * revoke tokens immediately, 
  * enqueue deletion jobs for object-store keys and metadata, 
  * mark records in analytics as "deleted" and exclude them from downstream exports, 
  * emit a signed audit event (JSON with timestamp, account id, deletion scope) and a human-readable certificate on completion.

- 30-day irreversible deletion offering: technically possible but requires an additional retention override on backups (shorter snapshot window) and a marketplace contract addendum; we should estimate operational cost and pass-through pricing to StellarCloud.

Driving questions for commercial: do we want to offer the 30-day deletion option as a standard marketplace tier or as an add-on?

Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

- For go-to-market, StellarCloud prefers (if available) the 30-day irreversible deletion option as an add-on for customers who purchase the "compliance" package. Please include a short price markup for that add-on.
- Finally, can you supply the signed deletion event example (redacted) so our compliance team can see the audit fields?

Attaching our draft tech spec for the listing to give context (attachment: Marketplace_Tech_Specs_DRAFT.docx). If you can get the attestation and playbook to me by EOD Friday (June 25) we can keep the publishing slot.

Best,
Devon
